subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should `openclaw.json` config env entries such as `env.KIMI_API_KEY` be a supported durable provider-auth source for systemd-managed Gateway turns, or should managed services steer users to `.env`/auth profiles instead?
rationale: The code and docs currently point in different directions: docs present config env as valid, snapshot reads apply it, but service-env planning intentionally avoids embedding literal config env values and the reporter saw runtime/status divergence.

options.title: Support config env in managed Gateway
options.body: Keep the documented config env path valid and add the missing service/runtime/status proof without storing secrets unsafely in unit files.

options.title: Prefer `.env` or auth profiles
options.body: Document config env as non-durable for managed services and update status output so it does not imply Gateway runtime auth will work from that source.

options.title: Split foreground and service semantics
options.body: Allow config env for foreground/CLI runs but require `.env`, SecretRef, or auth profiles for supervised Gateway installs, with explicit warnings.

recommendation.title: Support config env in managed Gateway
recommendation.body: Keep the documented config env path valid and add the missing service/runtime/status proof without storing secrets unsafely in unit files.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent config IO/service-env history and merged the adjacent service-env preservation fix, making them the best available owner for the credential-contract decision.
